claims.text: Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys is governed by formation of a coherent nanoscale precipitate structure.
A coherent nanoscale precipitate structure enhances high-temperature strength.
A coherent nanoscale precipitate structure enhances environmental resistance.
A coherent nanoscale precipitate structure enhances radiation tolerance.
A coherent nanoscale precipitate structure enhances cryogenic toughness.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates reduce lattice strain.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates increase grain-boundary cohesion.
Reduced lattice strain and increased grain-boundary cohesion enhance phase stability.
The precipitate-containing alloy will have 20% greater yield strength at 1000°C than the baseline alloy without coherent nanoscale precipitates.
The precipitate-containing alloy will have 30% greater toughness at 77 K than the baseline alloy without coherent nanoscale precipitates.
The proposed hypothesis applies when each of Al, Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni is present in the range 10–30 at.%.
The exact composition required to form the coherent nanoscale precipitate structure is unknown.
The processing conditions required to form the coherent nanoscale precipitate structure are unknown.
The effects of irradiation on phase stability are not well understood.
The proposed in situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction experiment spans 0–10 GPa and 25–1000°C.
The hypothesis is to be falsified if yield-strength improvement at 1000°C is below 10% or toughness improvement at 77 K is below 10%.

contradictions.description: The stated 25–1000°C experimental range does not include the specified cryogenic toughness condition of 77 K, and no irradiation exposure or dose is included despite claiming irradiated conditions.

The intervention is an observational X-ray diffraction method rather than a controlled processing change that creates or suppresses coherent precipitates, so it does not define how the precipitate-containing material is produced relative to the precipitate-free baseline.

The predictions are 20% strength and 30% toughness improvements, but falsification occurs only below 10%; results between 10% and the predicted values would neither satisfy the prediction nor falsify the hypothesis.
